review_notes:
I read the whole file, which holds one theorem, `eventually_boundary_weighted_scale`. I also read its upstream lemma `eventually_boundaryPairCount_le` in BoundaryCoverageCounts.lean and its use in BoundaryCoverage.lean. I grepped the Supply directory for other uses of the 1/100 exponent.

The only candidate was the hard-coded exponent 1/100. The proof would go through for any exponent a with 0 < a < 1/40, because the count bound gives X^(19/20+a)·log^4 X and the target needs X^(1-a)/log X. The count lemma itself fixes the exponent 19/20, and the only caller (BoundaryCoverage.lean) supplies exactly 1/100 through the weight-scale lemmas. That makes the specialisation tied to the pipeline rather than gratuitous. Generalising it would also mean reworking the rpow arithmetic and the exponent 3/100 in the little-o step, and I found no other user that would benefit. The other hypotheses (0 ≤ M, η > 0, the real types of M and U) are already as general as the proof needs. I therefore report no finding. My remaining uncertainty is whether other files outside the Supply directory would use a different exponent, and I did not search them.
